Subject: High latency and 5xxs in AZ2 — need urgent routing fallback

Nikhil,

We started seeing a sustained latency increase across our API calls to your hosted endpoint in AZ2 starting ~08:45 PDT. Error rate jumped to ~3.6% 5xx (mainly 502 / 504) and tail latency for chat completions spiked to 2.3s p95 from our normal ~350ms. This is impacting our sign-in flows and realtime inference for our glucose-alert predictions.

We opened a support ticket but need confirmation on whether Redwood can fail traffic to another region (USW2) while you investigate — we have no internal switch to rehome traffic immediately. Can you provide an estimated ETA and whether a geo-drain for our account is possible now? We will need a short comms message for our ops teams and an ask around potential credit for the incident window if SLA is breached.

Attached: quick KPI snapshot from our side.

— Angela

Subject: Re: High latency and 5xxs in AZ2 — need urgent routing fallback

Angela — thanks for the heads up and the snapshot. We see the same signal on our telemetry: AZ2 (us-west-2a) is reporting elevated CPU on several dedicated pods serving your tenant and a routing queue backlog in the AZ's ingress plane. Error profile matches 502/504 gateway timeouts.

Immediate plan (recommendation):
- Authorize a controlled geo-drain of new sessions from AZ2 to USW2 for your account only (no full account move). This will start steering new connections within 60–90s and allow in-flight requests to finish.
- Keep one small canary pool in AZ2 (reduced weight) to allow session stickiness for long-lived clients while we validate recovery.
- If AZ2 does not stabilize in 15 minutes, escalate to a full regional cutover and increase USW2 capacity for your routes.

We will also:
- Open an incident bridge (INC-20290614-72) with infra and runtime;
- Capture token-level latency and error breakdowns and provide a customer-facing status line;
- Prepare a credit estimate tied to ingress QPS during the impact window.

I need exec authorization to perform the geo-drain for Tidepool (this will incur cross-region routing for a subset of traffic and temporary overprovisioning in USW2). Asking Lauren and Marcus to weigh in.

ETA for the geo-drain activation after approval: ~2–3 minutes to push routing policies, with full gradual shift ~2 minutes per 10% weight change.

Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
